newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals lower after overnight falls.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals lower after overnight falls.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended lower across the board on Tuesday, after spot gold fell to a 20-month low of around $373 in New York overnight, traders said.
Spot November gold futures contract expired at noon at 1,356 yen per gram with 141 lots of deliveries.
Other prices ranged from two yen to five yen per gram lower, with the benchmark October contract ending down three at 1,338 yen.
Bullion was easier, quoted at $374.00/30 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against New York close of $374.35/85.
Market players hold bearish views on spot gold prices, while they added the outlook for gold futures mainly hinged on the currency market.

Private investors, hunted for bargains earlier in the day, retreated to the sidelines later ahead of the release of the Bank of Japan's quarterly corporate survey on Wednesday, to look for any impact on the currency market.
"The gold futures market is vulnerable to any rebound of the yen against the dollar," one trader said.
The market was also focusing on over-the-counter options expiry in New York later in the day.
"The gold market is overwhelmingly short. But any rebound led by funds' short-covering could be short-lived unless the U.S. stock market goes through a correction," another trader said.
Platinum futures was off early lows, supported by private investors's bargain-hunting buying.
Benchmark October platinum was off six yen per gram at 1,367 yen. Benchmark October silver was down 3.3 yen per 10 grams at 175.1 yen. Benchmark October palladium was six yen lower at 421 yen.
